Farhadi, MD Pre-procedure Diagnosis Right L5 radiculopathy, L4-L5 disc protrusion Post-procedure Diagnosis Same Procedure Right L5-S1 transforaminal epidural steroid injection under fluoroscopic guidance (CPT 64483) Anesthesia Local, 1% lidocaine. No sedation. Complications None

Patient with imaging-confirmed right paracentral L4-L5 disc protrusion and clinically corroborated right L5 radiculopathy, refractory to eight weeks of oral medication and fourteen sessions of physical therapy. Risks, benefits, and alternatives including continued conservative care and surgical decompression were discussed. Written informed consent obtained.

Patient placed prone on the fluoroscopy table with a bolster beneath the abdomen. The lumbosacral region was prepped with chlorhexidine and draped in sterile fashion. Under intermittent fluoroscopic guidance the target foramen was identified and the C-arm obliqued to visualize the 'Scotty dog' view. Skin and subcutaneous tissue infiltrated with 1% lidocaine. A 22-gauge spinal needle was advanced under intermittent fluoroscopy to the safe triangle beneath the pedicle. Position confirmed on AP and lateral views. Negative aspiration for blood and cerebrospinal fluid. Omnipaque 180 contrast, 1 mL, injected demonstrating appropriate epidural and perineural spread along the nerve root without vascular uptake. A solution of dexamethasone 10 mg with 1 mL of 0.25% bupivacaine was then injected slowly. The patient tolerated the injection well and reported his typical radicular pain reproduced on contrast injection, then relieved.

Patient monitored in recovery for 30 minutes. Motor and sensory function intact bilaterally. Ambulated without difficulty. Discharged home in stable condition with a responsible adult driver. Pre-procedure pain 7/10. Immediate post-procedure pain 2/10 (anesthetic phase).

PLAN – Pain diary for 14 days. – Resume physical therapy in 3 days. – Follow up in 3 weeks. May consider a second injection if partial but incomplete relief. – Return to Dr. Halloway if relief is inadequate to discuss surgical options. Electronically signed: Darius Farhadi, MD | 04/23/2024 14: 35

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS Right L4-L5 herniated nucleus pulposus with right L5 radiculopathy, failed conservative management.

POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS Same, confirmed intraoperatively.

PROCEDURE PERFORMED Right L4-L5 hemilaminotomy with microdiscectomy and decompression of the right L5 nerve root (CPT 63030).

INDICATIONS The patient is a 37-year-old male with a right L4-L5 disc protrusion causing right L5 radiculopathy with motor deficit, which has failed a course of physical therapy, oral neuropathic and anti-inflammatory medication, and one transforaminal epidural steroid injection. Symptoms have persisted for approximately seven months. Risks, benefits, and alternatives were reviewed and informed consent obtained.

symptoms have persisted for approximately seven months. risks, benefits, and alternatives were reviewed and informed consent obtained.

DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE The patient was brought to the operating room and general anesthesia was induced without difficulty. He was turned prone onto a Wilson frame with all pressure points padded. A surgical time-out was performed confirming patient identity, procedure, and correct operative level and laterality. The lumbar region was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. A localizing radiograph confirmed the L4-L5 interspace. A midline incision was made and carried through subcutaneous tissue. Subperiosteal dissection was carried out on the right side exposing the L4 lamina and L4-L5 interlaminar space. A retractor was placed and a repeat radiograph confirmed the level. Using the operating microscope, a hemilaminotomy of the inferior margin of the right L4 lamina was performed with a high-speed burr and Kerrison rongeurs. The ligamentum flavum was incised and removed. The thecal sac and traversing right L5 nerve root were identified. The nerve root was noted to be tented and erythematous over a firm extruded disc fragment in the right lateral recess. The nerve root was gently retracted medially. The fragment was delivered with a pituitary rongeur and additional loose degenerative nucleus pulposus was removed from the disc space. The lateral recess and foramen were then probed and found to be widely decompressed. The nerve root was noted to be freely mobile. Hemostasis was obtained with bipolar cautery and thrombin-soaked Gelfoam. The wound was irrigated with antibiotic solution.
